new_regressions.title: Async forwarder errors now visible for ~1 frame during typing — the exact context where they occur
new_regressions.description: F-7's clear-on-next-keypress TTL (new in 4ff5b94, main.rs:1105-1108 — no exemption for chat focus or async-origin messages) is applied to a channel that is NOT keypress-synchronized. Forwarder failures ('Forward failed: …', forwarder.rs:45) are written to the async sink and drained into app.status_message once per tick (main.rs:931-934). The tick order is: drain sink → draw (main.rs:944) → process buffered key events (clear at 1105-1108). A user whose keystrokes are failing to forward is by definition actively typing in chat, so the error is rendered for exactly one frame (~16ms at the active cadence, PREVIEW_ACTIVE_MS=16, main.rs:877) before their next in-flight keystroke wipes it. The same mechanism means any handler-set notice ('Killed X', 'Created X', 'Pasted N chars') that is set and followed by another buffered key inside the same 8ms drain batch (main.rs:1076-1087) is cleared before EVER being drawn — draw happens once per tick, before the batch. At baseline f432154 status_message had no expiry: on non-Sessions tabs these notices persisted until replaced (e.g. error lands, user switches to Settings → baseline showed the error there; HEAD shows the per-tab hint instead). The fix commit claims forwarder errors are now surfaced; for the typing user the surfacing is ~16ms, i.e. still effectively invisible.

new_regressions.title: F-1 vanish notice 'X ended — back to list' is wiped by the user's own in-flight keystroke — unreadable exactly when it matters
new_regressions.description: Both halves are fix-series additions: the notice was introduced by 8ea3a4a (F-1) and the clear-on-keypress TTL by 4ff5b94 (F-7). When the chat-focused session vanishes, the 2s housekeeping refresh (main.rs:2033-2036) drops focus to List and sets '{name} ended — back to list' (app.rs:1774). The target audience of this notice is a user mid-typing into the dead session — their very next keystroke (already in flight) hits the TTL clear at main.rs:1105-1108, erasing the only explanation of why the focus jumped, AND dispatches into list mode where letters are commands ('x' kill, 'c' new session…). A keypress-heavy user gets a silent focus jump plus a stray list command, with the explanatory notice on screen for one keystroke interval at most. The F-1 focus-drop itself is correct; the notice that makes it comprehensible has a TTL of zero for the user it was written for. (Per L1 this is code-inspection reasoning, not a runtime repro — the timing window is structural: clear fires on every non-Release key event unconditionally.)

new_regressions.title: Sessions-tab git status (`↑4h • main`) now hidden behind the per-tab hint / 'Refreshed' ack on every tab arrival and F5
new_regressions.description: At baseline f432154 the Sessions-tab status bar gave git text absolute priority ('Some(g) => git'), so the compact git status was visible the instant the user landed on the tab. At HEAD the F-7 priority swap (ui.rs:3216-3219, Some(status_message) always wins) interacts with the pre-existing per-tab hint seeding that fires on EVERY tab switch (main.rs:1991-1999) and the F5 'Refreshed' ack (main.rs:1409): each arrival on Sessions now shows the long keyboard hint ('↑/↓ select · Enter/Tab chat · c/C/g new agent…') or 'Refreshed' instead of the git status, until the user presses one more key to consume the notice. A glance-at-git-status-after-switching workflow that worked at baseline now requires an extra keypress. The fix commit explicitly acknowledges the hint seeding and chose the TTL over de-seeding the hint, so this is a designed tradeoff — but it is a real behavior regression vs f432154, and de-seeding navigation hints (or letting git text outrank pure-hint messages) would have avoided it.

new_regressions.title: Alt+Esc escape hatch is unreachable at runtime — no way left to send a literal ESC to the agent (AF-1 dead on arrival)
new_regressions.citation: crates/omega-tui/src/input.rs:1858 (KeyCode::Esc if alt arm), crates/omega-cli/src/main.rs:717-722 (raw mode + alt screen + mouse only; no PushKeyboardEnhancementFlags anywhere in crates/ — grep returns zero hits), crossterm-0.29.0/src/event/sys/unix/parse.rs:77 (ESC ESC parsed as plain KeyCode::Esc with KeyModifiers::NONE), Cargo.lock (omega-tui -> crossterm 0.29.0), input.rs:2330-2342 (test passes only via synthetic ALT KeyEvent)
new_regressions.description: F-2 (5cf827b) removed the baseline behavior where plain Esc in chat focus forwarded "Escape" to the agent PTY, and 4ff5b94 added Alt+Esc as the replacement (input.rs:1858). But the TUI never enables the kitty/CSI-u keyboard-enhancement protocol (terminal init at main.rs:717-722 is raw-mode-only), so every legacy-mode terminal — including Termius/SSH, the project's stated client — emits Alt+Esc as the byte pair ESC ESC, which crossterm 0.29.0 explicitly parses as a PLAIN Esc with no ALT modifier (parse.rs:77). The result: Alt+Esc falls into the plain-Esc arm and exits chat to the session list; the `KeyCode::Esc if alt` forward arm is unreachable from real keyboard input. Net effect introduced by the fix series: there is NO path at HEAD to deliver a literal ESC to the agent from chat focus — vim insert-mode exit, less, Claude Code's own Esc-to-interrupt, and every modal CLI inside a session are silently broken (baseline f432154 forwarded Esc, so they all worked). The Help tab actively mis-advertises the dead binding (ui.rs:2969 "Alt+Esc — Send a literal ESC to the agent (vim/less)"). Worse fragmentation case: if the two ESC bytes arrive in separate reads over SSH, the first parses as Esc (chat→list) and the second hits the Sessions-tab quit arm (input.rs:1556) — Alt+Esc can quit the whole TUI. The 4ff5b94 regression test chat_alt_esc_forwards_literal_escape (input.rs:2330-2342) gives false confidence: it constructs KeyEvent::new(KeyCode::Esc, KeyModifiers::ALT) synthetically, a value the shipped parser never produces (L1: runtime is the only truth). Fix options: push crossterm's KeyboardEnhancementFlags at init (with graceful fallback), or pick a chord the legacy parser can actually deliver (e.g. a Ctrl-based prefix).

new_regressions.title: Alt+Esc / Ctrl+C recovery path is Help-tab-only — zero in-context discoverability at the moment a vim/less user's Esc muscle memory breaks
new_regressions.citation: crates/omega-tui/src/ui.rs:2969 (only surface mentioning Alt+Esc), ui.rs:776 (chat title hint: "CHAT (Esc → list to manage)" — no Alt+Esc/Ctrl+C), crates/omega-tui/src/input.rs:1868 (Esc status message: only "Focus: session list"), input.rs:1104 and input.rs:1786-1790 (enter-chat / Tab status hints — no Alt+Esc)
new_regressions.description: Even assuming the Alt+Esc binding worked, the fix series changed a silent always-worked behavior (baseline: Esc forwarded to the agent) into a focus jump, and surfaced the replacement only in the Help tab key list (ui.rs:2969). Every in-context surface a user actually sees while chat-focused omits it: the list-panel title hint (ui.rs:776), the focus-change status message emitted by the new Esc handler ("Focus: session list", input.rs:1868), the enter-chat hint (input.rs:1104), and the Tab-transition hints (input.rs:1786-1790). A vim user pressing Esc is yanked to the session list with a message that explains what happened but not how to get an ESC into the agent (Alt+Esc) or interrupt it (Ctrl+C) — they must leave their task and read the Help tab to recover a keystroke that worked unprompted at f432154. The handler's own doc comment names the recovery keys (input.rs:1644-1645) but that text is invisible to users. Minimal fix: extend the Esc status message at input.rs:1868 to e.g. "Focus: session list (Alt+Esc = ESC to agent, Ctrl+C = interrupt)" and/or add Alt+Esc to the chat-side title hint at ui.rs:776.
